commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Bond
commitResults.messageBody: Update the Java entry point, startup banner, and documentation so the project consistently uses the new chatbot name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add initial Bond greeting and farewell
commitResults.messageBody: Display the chatbot banner, greet the user, and exit with a farewell message as required.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command echo and bye handling
Add task storing capability and list command
Add task completion status with mark command
Task data changed to  Task class
Move Java classes into bond package
commitResults.messageBody:
The Java classes use the default package, which does not follow the
project's coding standard and makes the source structure unclear.

Move Bond and Task into the bond package and align their Javadocs
with the SE-EDU Java conventions without changing chatbot behavior.

Java changes need a consistent, project-specific interpretation of
the SE-EDU basic and intermediate coding rules.

Add a reusable skill with the applicable rules and require agents to
load it whenever they create, edit, refactor, or review Java code.

Commit and branch conventions need to remain consistent across future
agent work.

Add a reusable skill for SE-EDU Git rules and require agents to load it
when preparing commits or branch names. Preserve explicit authorization
for committing and pushing.

Keep generic tasks available while introducing Todo as a separate task type.

This provides the first Level 4 increment before applying inheritance.

Let users create time-sensitive missions.

Keep dates and times as strings for this incremental implementation.

Let users record missions that occur during a specified time period.

Keep event dates and times as strings for this incremental implementation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor task types to use inheritance
commitResults.messageBody:
Todo, Deadline, and Event repeat common task behavior.

Reuse Task as their parent so each subtype only handles its own details.

Add a reusable project skill and test plan for checking console
commands against their expected output.

Require agents to review the plan and run the UI tests after code
changes so user-visible regressions are caught promptly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bond: Extract command handling from main
commitResults.messageBody:
Bond's main method handles startup, command selection, input parsing,
task mutation, and response rendering in one place. Readers must track
several responsibilities and abstraction levels through a long method.

Extract the session loop and command-specific operations into focused
helper methods. Keep main at the lifecycle level so the program flow is
clear, while each command's existing parsing and output stay together.

This preserves observable behavior while making future command changes
easier to locate, understand, and review.

Todo, deadline, and event commands repeat the same storage, counting,
pluralization, and confirmation-output logic. Keeping those copies in
sync makes later changes harder and creates avoidable inconsistency risk.

Route all three task types through one helper after their command-specific
fields have been parsed. This retains the distinct parsing logic while
keeping the shared addition workflow in one place.

The refactoring preserves all command behavior and console output.

Command recognition uses string literals while argument extraction relies
on matching numeric offsets. A prefix change can therefore leave parsing
silently out of sync with command detection.

Define each command prefix once and derive argument boundaries from the
selected prefix's length. This makes the relationship explicit and removes
unexplained substring positions without changing the command grammar.

The refactoring preserves all existing input and output behavior.

Bond passes a task array and a separate count through its command
handlers. Those values describe one collection but can be changed or
passed independently, making invalid combinations possible.

Introduce TaskList to own the array, size, capacity, insertion, and
lookup operations. Update Bond to depend on that abstraction instead of
managing the collection representation itself.

Add the new source file to the documented UI-test build command. Console
behavior remains unchanged and all UI cases continue to pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bond: Separate UI and command parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
Bond still owns console rendering and command interpretation alongside
application control. This mixes responsibilities and forces changes to
input syntax or output wording through the central coordinator.

Introduce Ui for console interaction, Parser for command recognition and
argument conversion, and CommandType for explicit dispatch. Keep Bond
focused on coordinating parsed operations with the task list.

Update the documented build command for the new source files. The change
preserves existing commands and output, verified by every UI test case.

Task exposes its description and completion state to every subclass even
though none requires direct field access. This widens the mutation surface
and makes the class responsible for fewer of its own invariants.

Make both fields private and make the description final because it does
not change after construction. Continue exposing completion changes only
through the existing mark and unmark operations.

This tightens encapsulation without changing task behavior or output.

Unknown input was stored as a generic task instead of being rejected.

Introduce BondException and centralized recovery. Invalid commands show
actionable feedback without ending the session.

Malformed task commands could create incomplete tasks or terminate Bond.

Validate each required component and report a specific correction.
Reject invalid tasks before they reach the task list.

Invalid mark and unmark numbers could terminate Bond or access outside
the task list.

Validate selection syntax and bounds before retrieving a mission.
Explain each rejected order without changing mission state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Guard against a full task list
commitResults.messageBody:
The fixed task array could overflow when a 101st mission was added.

Reject additions once the dossier reaches its 100-mission capacity.
Report a recoverable error instead of terminating Bond.
Integrate the completed error-handling increment into master.

The growing codebase keeps classes with different responsibilities
in one package.

Separate parsing, task, UI, and exception classes into focused
packages while retaining Bond as the entry point. Update the UI test
build command to compile Java sources recursively.

Allow users to delete a mission by its list number.

Report the removed mission and updated count for clear feedback.

Replace the fixed-size task array with a dynamically sized collection.

Preserve task operations while allowing more than 100 missions.

Persist the task list after successful add, mark, and unmark commands.

Use a simple text format so startup loading can be added separately.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load tasks from disk at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Restore saved task types and completion statuses when Bond starts.

Treat a missing data file as an empty task list.

Add UI coverage for persistence across application restarts.

Report malformed archives and file-access failures without raw exceptions.

Use safe file replacement and roll back task changes when saving fails.

Escape storage delimiters and cover failure cases with UI fixtures.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a portable relative data path
commitResults.messageBody:
Construct the relative task-data path from separate components.

Reject absolute storage paths to keep project behavior portable.

Preserve first-run creation of the missing data directory and file.

Integrate task deletion from the parallel Level 6 branch.

Include the A-Collections task-storage extension.

Integrate disk-backed storage from the parallel Level 7 branch.

Preserve deletion while saving every task-list change.

Include startup loading and corrupted-file recovery.

Configure Gradle and Shadow to package Bond as an executable JAR.

Include the Gradle wrapper for reproducible builds.

Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList already separate the main concerns,
but Bond passes the same session objects through its static command
methods. This obscures which object owns the application state.

Give Bond its own UI, storage, and task-list fields and a constructor
that accepts the relative archive path. Move the application lifecycle
into run and let main construct and launch a single Bond instance.
Use instance methods for operations that need this session state.

Keep loading in run so the welcome message, startup failure handling,
input cleanup, and save-failure rollback retain their existing behavior.
Leave Parser as a stateless utility and avoid adding unnecessary classes.

Validate with Java 25.0.4.1 and all 20 cases in test/ui-test-plan.md,
including persistence across restarts and rollback after failed saves.
The existing test plan requires no changes for this refactor.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract ListCommand behind an abstract Command
commitResults.messageBody:
Bond dispatches commands and performs their operations itself. Introduce
a shared Command abstraction so operations can move into separate classes
in small, independently verifiable steps.

Move the list operation into ListCommand and invoke it through Command
from Bond. Keep display formatting in Ui and leave parsing and the other
operations unchanged. Starting with a read-only operation establishes the
execution contract without moving persistence or rollback logic yet.

Accept tasks, UI, and storage through the common execute method so later
commands can use the same calling convention, even though listing does
not need storage. Defer exit signaling and Parser.parse until their
corresponding commands are extracted.

Compile with Java 25.0.4.1 and run UI-1 through UI-20 sequentially: all
28 sessions and 215 inputs match the existing output and data assertions.
Leave the UI plan unchanged because its existing cases cover this
behavior-preserving extraction.

Bond still owns the add, save, and rollback workflow even though command
execution now has a shared abstraction. Move that workflow together into
AddCommand so the main class can gradually become a command coordinator.

Accept a parsed Task in the command constructor and reuse one command for
todos, deadlines, and events. Keep syntax validation and task creation in
Parser, and keep output formatting in Ui. This avoids coupling execution
to the original input text or duplicating logic for each task type.

Preserve the order of operations: append the task, save the list, then
confirm success. Remove the unsaved addition and propagate the storage
error if saving fails, leaving the existing in-memory list intact.

Compile with Java 25.0.4.1 and run UI-1 through UI-20 sequentially. All
28 sessions and 215 inputs pass, including saved task reloads and the
failed-add rollback case. The existing UI plan needs no changes because
this extraction preserves the commands, output, and storage behavior.

Bond still owns deletion and its persistence recovery logic. Move the
complete workflow into DeleteCommand to continue separating command
execution from application coordination in a small, reviewable step.

Accept an index that Parser has already validated and execute the command
immediately against the session's task list. Keep command syntax and
selection errors in Parser, and leave confirmation formatting in Ui.

Save the shortened list before reporting success. If saving fails,
restore the same task at its original index and propagate the storage
error so both task order and completion status remain intact.

Compile with Java 25.0.4.1 and run UI-1 through UI-20 sequentially. All
28 sessions and 215 inputs pass with exact output and data-file matches,
including deletion across restarts and restoration after a failed save.
Keep the existing UI plan unchanged because its cases already cover
the behavior preserved by this extraction.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract mark and unmark command classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Bond still changes task completion status and handles save failures
directly. Move these workflows into MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand so
every task operation now executes through the Command abstraction.

Give each command a validated task index, leaving input validation in
Parser and response formatting in Ui. Save before reporting success and
remember the previous status so a failed write restores the task rather
than blindly reversing its status. Remove the operation methods and
rollback helper from Bond.

Keep two small, explicit command classes instead of introducing another
inheritance layer for their similar save-and-rollback steps. This keeps
the behavior easy to follow at the cost of a little duplication.

Compile with Java 25.0.4.1 and run UI-1 through UI-20 sequentially. All
28 sessions and 215 inputs match the expected output and file contents,
including status persistence and failed mark/unmark rollback. The
existing UI test plan covers this behavior-preserving extraction and
requires no changes.

Bond handles bye outside the command abstraction, so the loop must know
which command ends the session. Add Command.isExit with a false default
and let ExitCommand display the farewell and return true.

Create each command before executing it through one shared path, then
use its exit flag to control the loop. Keep command construction in Bond
for now so moving parsing into Parser remains a separate increment.

Print the closing divider in the loop's finally block for every command
response. Remove it from Ui.showGoodbyeMessage to preserve the exact
farewell output without printing the divider twice. Keep input cleanup
and startup error handling in the existing application lifecycle.

Compile with Java 25.0.4.1 and run UI-1 through UI-20 sequentially. All
28 sessions and 215 inputs match the expected output and file contents,
including immediate exit, exit after errors, and persistence across
restarts. The existing UI plan already covers the preserved behavior.

Bond still selects concrete command classes and owns unknown-command
errors. Move this responsibility into Parser.parse so the application
loop only reads input, parses a command, executes it, and checks isExit.

Accept the current task count alongside the input to preserve existing
task-selection validation without giving Parser access to the task list.
Execute each returned command immediately, before the list can change.
Keep the parser's type, index, and task helpers private now that callers
use the single parse entry point.

Remove command-specific imports, the construction switch, and parsing
messages from Bond. Keep loading, error display, dividers, and input
cleanup in the application lifecycle. This completes the planned command
extraction while preserving the console and persistence behavior.

Compile with Java 25.0.4.1 and run UI-1 through UI-20 sequentially. All
28 sessions and 215 inputs match the expected output and file contents,
covering command validation, execution, exit, persistence, and rollback.
The existing UI plan requires no changes for this refactor.

Store deadline dates as LocalDate so the app can validate real calendar dates and display them consistently. Require yyyy-MM-dd input and keep that format in the archive while showing a readable month name in the UI.

Report invalid dates from commands and saved archives clearly. Update the console test plan and fixtures for the new behavior.
Add Level 8 date handling to deadlines

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Task descriptions cannot be searched, making missions harder to locate as the list grows. Add a read-only find command that matches descriptions regardless of case and retains original mission numbers for later mark or delete commands.

Validate missing keywords and cover matches, misses, and unchanged storage in the UI test plan.
Add Level 9 Find command

The exit and list commands have public methods without JavaDoc,
leaving the A-JavaDoc stretch goal incomplete. Document their
behavior and parameters so all non-private classes and methods,
and non-trivial private methods, have header comments.
Complete A-JavaDoc stretch goal

The docs page contains placeholders, leaving users without instructions.

Explain startup, commands, mission status, and saved data for new users.

commitResults.messageBody:
A finite input stream crashes Bond after its last command.

Check for another line before reading, and add a UI case for EOF.
